body: I think we should try to use data from https://github.com/Z-Anatomy/Models-of-human-anatomy, if we didn't already. So we can reproduce the precise acoustically affecting part of mouth and breathing organs.
We also need to try rebuilding 3D model based on research at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12440228
We also should try to use https://github.com/diku-dk/Open-Full-Jaw for maximum detail model, we always can scale down from maximum detailed model.

We also need to integrate the most accurate data from https://humanatlas.io, for example https://apps.humanatlas.io/kg-explorer/ref-organ/mouth-male/v1.0

We should slice our 3D model as MRI does, if we have reference MRI, and we should be able to compare key points automatically when possible.

If the source of models already in 3D, we should incorporate all of them to increase quality, and make configurable flexible simulator that allows to switch between all variations between gathered 3D models by configuration of any part of them.

Meaning we should generalize.

We may also need to use ideas from meta human (Unreal Engine) and other formats.

And we should have head only adapter demoes for these, like we did in https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar (yet there the voice generation and voice animation was done completely wrong).

We should be able to have automated bridges to different formats of character models to simulate correctly talking animation, that is actually anatomically correct.

So by providing best possible level of detail as the basis and carefully scale it down to multiple simplier levels, we should be able to have GPU optimized simulation of sound on high end GPUs and simple yet working acoustic and animation simulation on less powerful GPUs and CPUs.

Also check we fully deliver on:
- https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/pull/10#issuecomment-6248419847
- https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/pull/10#issuecomment-6248312336
- https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/pull/10#issuecomment-6248264362
